text:
The central conflict in the text revolves around the clash between economic greed and cultural preservation. Jacob, a prospector, discovers gold on sacred indigenous land, which immediately pits him against the local tribe's chief who is determined to protect his people's heritage. This personal and moral dilemma is exacerbated by external pressures, as outsiders learn of the discovery, forcing Jacob to choose between his loyalty to the potential wealth and his moral obligations to the indigenous community.

The longest river in the world is the Nile River.
